test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 22 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below:

Sarah and Fidaa entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.

options.text: Sarah and Fidaa are entering into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidaa will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidaa had entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidaa were entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Sarah and Fidaa will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **simple past tense**: “entered into an agreement.”
 
• To change it to the **simple future tense**, the correct structure is: **Subject + will + base verb**.
 
• In this case: “Sarah and Fidaa **will enter** into an agreement...” correctly indicates an action that is expected to happen in the future.
 
• The phrase “that are currently accessible” remains unchanged as it refers to present conditions.

Correct sentence: *Sarah and Fidaa **will enter** into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "are entering"** – Present continuous tense, not future.
 
• **Option 3: "had entered"** – Past perfect tense, refers to an action completed before another past action.
 
• **Option 4: "were entered"** – Grammatically incorrect; “entered” is not used in passive voice with “were” in this context.
